title: Vikrant Massey Turns 'Musafir Cafe' Into Real Hill Cafés in Himachal and Uttarakhand
excerpt: The actor's production house Homemade Stories is building two replicas of the show's café — plus around 20 artist-residency rooms — extending the Netflix series' world beyond the screen.
body:
• Actor Vikrant Massey is turning the fictional Musafir Cafe from his Netflix series into real cafés, with two locations under construction in Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
  • The cafés are being designed as replicas of the one seen in the show, and the project includes around 20 rooms reserved as artist residencies.
  • The venture runs through Homemade Stories, the production house Massey founded with his wife Sheetal Thakur — who is herself from Himachal Pradesh.
  • Musafir Cafe, which began streaming on Netflix on July 24, 2026, follows Massey's character Chander as he leaves city life to build a café in the hills; a second season has been announced.

From screen to hillside

Vikrant Massey is taking Musafir Cafe beyond the screen. After the success of the Netflix web series, the actor is set to open two real-life Musafir Cafés — one in Himachal Pradesh and one in Uttarakhand — with construction already underway at both locations, according to reports. The cafés are being designed as replicas of the one seen in the show, extending the series' world into physical spaces in the hills.

A source close to the project told Bollywood Hungama: "Vikrant Massey is set to open two Musafir Cafés, one in Himachal Pradesh and the other in Uttarakhand. Construction is already underway at both locations. The cafés are being designed as replicas of the one seen in the show, and the project will also include around 20 rooms for artist residencies. It's an extension of the world of Musafir Cafe beyond the screen."

More than a café

The project goes beyond hospitality. The roughly 20 residency rooms will offer artists and creators a place to stay and work — a deliberate echo of the series' themes of creative retreat in the mountains. Exact locations, launch dates and operating details have not yet been revealed.

The venture is being developed through Homemade Stories, the production house Massey launched with his wife, actor Sheetal Thakur — a connection that makes the hill-state locations personal. Thakur hails from Shahtalai in Himachal Pradesh's Bilaspur district, and the couple married in traditional Himachali customs at her ancestral home in 2022. In the series, Massey plays Chander, a man who leaves city life for the mountains and builds his life around a café — art imitating life, and now life imitating art.

Why the show lent itself to this

Musafir Cafe, which began streaming on July 24, 2026, stars Massey alongside Vedika Pinto and Mahima Makwana, and is based on Divya Prakash Dubey's novel of the same name. The café became one of the show's defining elements — the setting fans kept asking about. The actual filming took place at Jharipani Castle, a heritage property in Mussoorie, Uttarakhand, which has itself become a minor pilgrimage site for fans since the show aired. Netflix has announced a second season with Massey, Pinto and Makwana returning.

The move fits a broader trend of Indian screen worlds spilling into real-world hospitality — but the artist-residency angle gives this one a distinct shape. Rather than pure themed dining, the plan positions the cafés as creative hubs where the mountains do what the show said they do: give artists room to work.

Homemade Stories' bigger bet

The cafés mark Massey's deepening shift from actor to entrepreneur-producer. He has said he wants Homemade Stories to serve as a platform for emerging storytellers and performers, contributing to the industry from behind the camera as well as in front of it — with Musafir Cafe as the banner's first production and the new hill cafés its first physical-world extension.

What's next

No opening dates have been announced, and with construction still in progress, the cafés are likely a 2027 story. For diaspora travellers heading to the hills — and for fans who already trek to the Jharipani Castle filming location — two more Musafir addresses are about to join the map.
